ink-black.$description: Ink Black — Primary text, pill CTA background, logo mark, icon strokes — near-black rather than pure black gives a softer, warmer feel than #000000

pure-black.$description: Pure Black — Occasional hard-black fills for high-contrast accents and announcement bar

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Body text, link color, secondary headings — warmer than Ink Black, used when pure black feels too heavy

slate-gray.$description: Slate Gray — Muted helper text, placeholder content, disabled states

hairline.$description: Hairline — Default border for cards, inputs, icons, nav separators, and table dividers — the most-used color in the entire system

cloud.$description: Cloud — Secondary card borders, subtle structural outlines

warm-canvas.$description: Warm Canvas — Page background — the slightly warm off-white that distinguishes this from a sterile pure-white SaaS look

pure-white.$description: Pure White — Card surfaces, button text, elevated panels — the layer above the warm canvas

mint-wash.$description: Mint Wash — Soft green-tinted surface wash for highlighted sections, tag backgrounds, subtle callout zones

bean-orange.$description: Bean Orange — Decorative squiggle strokes, inline icon accent, brand heartbeat — warm vivid orange that defines the playful personality

bean-green.$description: Bean Green — Decorative squiggle fills, inline icon accent, growth-positive visual cue — saturated mid-green for energy without screaming

bean-blue.$description: Bean Blue — Decorative squiggle outlines, inline icon accent — the third color in the confetti triad used sparingly

mint-border.$description: Mint Border — Green outline accent for tags, dividers, and focused UI edges

inter.$description: All text — single-family system. Hero at 64px/weight 600+ is the loudest element; body sits at 16-17px/weight 400. Inter is the obvious Notion-native choice, so it feels native to the product it serves. Weight 500 carries nav and button labels; 600-700 reserved for headlines.
